validated_results.title: Compliance with the 2018 World Cancer Research Fund/American Institute for Cancer Research Cancer Prevention Recommendations and Prostate Cancer.
validated_results.reason: Population-based case-control study investigating the association between alcohol consumption recommendation adherence and incident prostate cancer risk.

extraction.population: Men aged 40-80 years with incident prostate cancer and controls residing in the coverage area of the reference hospitals

sample_size.excerpt: Figure 1 shows the flow-chart diagram for the participants in the CAPLIFE study until December 2019. A total of 398 PCa cases and 302 controls had complete information for the 2018 WCRF/AICR score and a plausible total energy intake.
sample_size.location: Abstract; total_n derived from reported group counts 398 + 302 = 700

cases.excerpt: A total of 398 incident PCa cases and 302 controls were included.

effect_size.excerpt: Lower consumption of “fast foods’ and other processed foods high in fat, starches or sugars, and sugar-sweetened drinks were associated with a lower risk of PCa, aOR = 0.63 (95% CI 0.42–0.64) and aOR = 0.30 (95% CI 0.12–0.77), respectively ( p -trend < 0.05). Also, not consuming alcohol showed a protective association, aOR = 0.49 (95% CI 0.27–0.91) for men who met with the recommendations ( p -trend < 0.05).

design.excerpt: A population-based case-control study was developed to evaluate the association between lifestyles and PCa among Spanish men (CAPLIFE study).

timing.excerpt: We have only included incident cases before starting any type of treatment for PCa; (2) age between 40 and 80 years; (3) residence in the coverage area of the reference hospitals for 6 months or more prior to recruitment.

continent.excerpt: A population-based case-control study was developed to evaluate the association between lifestyles and PCa among Spanish men (CAPLIFE study).

exposure_measurement.excerpt: In addition, subjects were provided with a semi-quantitative food frequency questionnaire (FFQ); also previously validated for the Spanish population [ 35 ] which included 134 foods, specifying the portion size for each of them, referring to the 12 months prior to diagnosis.
